title: Achieved assurance record — v1.0
description: plan.md §8.1's 'Achieved:' worked example. One per obligation, machine-recorded by a verifier run into a work package's CI report (ci/results/WP-*.json, §10's `per_obligation_assurance_record: true`) -- never hand-authored or human-reviewed the way a normative file (e.g. an interaction's required_assurance) is: §7.2's human-checkpoint list names 'assurance-profile authorship' (the REQUIRED side), never achieved-record recording, since a human freely authoring what was 'achieved' would be indistinguishable from fabricating a verification result. No `review` block for the same reason evidence records carry none. Consumed by scripts/satisfies.py's satisfies(required_profile, achieved_record, context) -- chainlink #23.

kind.description: Verification-method category (plan.md §8.1's type split) -- never a claim value, never a trust/support state; the schema's own enum vocabulary keeps this disjoint from `claim.kind`.

scope.description: Verifier-specific scope keys (e.g. input_domain, unwind, harness_hash) -- deliberately open, mirroring docs/interaction-schema.json's own required_assurance.minimum_scope. satisfies() compares this against a required_profile's minimum_scope key-for-key, by exact string equality only -- no numeric ordering is inferred, since the vocabulary is not typed.

status.description: plan.md §16.4: a record with full witness coverage and zero verifier results is still `unsupported` -- satisfies() treats this as an unconditional failure, never something the other fields can outweigh.
